findings.description: The bucket is explicitly documented as public and has no ACL restriction, no bucket policy and no accompanying aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource, so public ACLs/policies are not blocked at the bucket level. Combined with the customer master data object written into it, this exposes sensitive data to anonymous readers.

No server_side_encryption_configuration block is declared, so objects (including customer-master.xlsx) are stored without customer-managed KMS encryption and with no enforced bucket-level default encryption.

A file named customer-master.xlsx (sensitive customer records) is uploaded into the publicly annotated, unencrypted 'data' bucket with no server_side_encryption or kms_key_id argument, and the source file is committed alongside the Terraform code.
Financial data bucket declares no server_side_encryption_configuration, so contents are stored without enforced default encryption or KMS key control.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is set on this bucket, leaving stored objects without an enforced encryption default or KMS key boundary.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is set, so data science datasets are stored without enforced default encryption, unlike the sibling logs bucket which uses aws:kms.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block guards this bucket; the private ACL alone does not prevent a later bucket policy or object ACL from making financial data publicly readable.
No bucket policy denying requests where aws:SecureTransport is false, so objects in this bucket may be retrieved over unencrypted HTTP.
